Its main aim is to turn the reader from an indifferent onlooker, or an empty-handed victim of the situation, into an aware and responsible person who holds on to their dignity: someone who changes their own thinking, ethics and conscience at the root before waiting for change from outside, and who moves, through shared and organised work, towards a lasting revival.

Mashkhally Zhyanawa is a roadmap for restoring trust and self-confidence to the members of our society, through self-education and self-organisation in a new political movement that brings people back to honest and legitimate politics and governance, for the happiness and wellbeing of our people, relying on the people’s own inexhaustible strength.

The book Mashkhally Zhyanawa, written and published in 2025 by Abdullah Mala Nuri, is an intellectual, political and social text that offers, in a critical and educational way, a deep reading of the reality of society and of the system of government in the Kurdistan Region. It does not stop at describing the crises: it identifies the structural and internal sources of Kurdish fragmentation and weakness, and sets out a roadmap the author calls “self-healing” and “the politics of self-healing”: returning will, awareness and responsibility to the individual and to society itself, instead of waiting in vain for a solution from outside or repeating old tactics that lead nowhere.

The book warns that online activity and careless likes cannot take the place of the street, organising on the ground and work in the field. It closes by stressing commitment to the manifesto and the roadmap, with the example of McDonald’s operating manual as Alain de Botton describes it, and names an organised movement, an economy of revival, and the protection of dignity and freedom as a new beginning.
